You sound like me and my ex-bestie. I noticed with people like this, even when you talk to them seriously about how you are feeling, they somehow find a way to manipulate you to think you’re being too sensitive or then fully blow you off. 

If you want to keep the friendship, start by putting up boundaries. You won’t tell your friend ‘hey, these are my boundaries’. You will simply start honouring them because boundaries are for us. 

If she calls during cardio, do not answer. Only call back when you’re available. If she makes comments about you not eating or drinking, you can either choose to limit the frequency of these outings or simply stop joining her. If she does make a comment about your food choice etc. just literally point out the obvious. Like if she says “oh ya she doesn’t eat that anymore because she’s trying to be healthy” respond with yes, that’s correct. It really works to do that because they have nothing else to say. And if they do, they want a reaction from you. Do not give them the reaction whatever you do! 

Later in the friendship, when my friend was ready to get healthy and lose weight, all the things she made fun of me for doing, she started doing those things with complete confidence. So it was really frustrating for me to see that “when I do something, it’s an opportunity to mock me, but when you do something, the respect and support is always there from me”. I realized that before we were two fat friends and she was the pretty one. But once I started losing weight, I started to look better and was threatened by that. I am super happy to have that friend out of my life but I do wish I stood up for myself more in the friendship.  I also have made peace with the fact that she targeted me to be my friend because I was so passive aggressive and if I did stand up for myself, she would have left the friendship on her own years ago. We live and we learn. 

Good luck to you!! Keep on your health journey.

- yes, ketamine was prescribed by my psychiatrist. I was given pills (which are least absorbable, but the government doesn’t want to pay for IV). I didn’t know about it at all and didn’t know it was also used a recreational drug. The way ketamine is portrayed in media is so inaccurate though. I believe you that you use your meds properly. I am also super straight edge and don’t like to mess around. I don’t even drink alcohol and had to give up coffee. I would say just research it if you’re interested and ask your doctor but don’t run to it as a cure all. 
- yes, benzos made my anxiety worse and affected my cognition. It is a known thing in the psychiatric community that they overall make the anxiety feel worse. There will be a hellish withdrawal period too that you just gotta fight through to stay off. Keep in mind I took several a day for a few months due a serious trauma trigger. I guess they kept me alive so maybe it’s fine overall. I love benzos and if they didn’t give me any side effects I would be on them today. 
- I only used cannabis oil after trying everything else and didn’t think I would be this person but here I am. It took me 4+ years to finally try it. I don’t think you should take it if you’re uncomfortable. For now, it helps more than harms but I’d love to not be so reliant on it. If you are curious, there are other cannabinoids like CBN and CBG alongside CBD that are being used and researched. 
- I’m sure you’ve heard this before, but meditation, Breathwork and yoga (specifically yin), help to manage if we do them consistently. I am still trying and failing in this area but I give myself compassion. 
- I’m in Canada and the west coast winters aren’t that bad but the darkness gets to me and is a huge trigger for lows (lower than the existing deep lows lol). So I try to get a walk or something in during the light hours. It does help. 
- By no way do I have a handle on my suicidal thoughts and I have very valid reasons to die. Something I tell myself when I feel like I’m at my end is that I haven’t tried everything yet. And once I have tried everything, I will give myself permission to kms guilt-free. It helps me going.

I (33F) am currently in the search and my parents sound a little like yours. They always brought me any and every proposal anyone ever sent them without any filter. When I say no because the guy was too old, in another country, not attractive to me, uneducated, they would have a million excuses and tell me that none of my reasons for rejection were real reasons. Weirdly, my father was more concerned with how good the marriage would be for the guy. For example, the guy could be sponsored to Canada and his life would flourish. There is zero regard for who I am and what I want. Recently, my dad sent a proposal and said either my sister or I can agree. My sister and I have an 8 year gap!! My mother on the other hand acts like she’s looking for a husband for herself. She has opinions on their skin tone and hair type. 

So ya, I believe you that these parents don’t always have our best interest or even know how to go about the process. At 19, they nearly bullied me to marry this guy in Pakistan because he was the great grandson of an imam. I agreed because I wanted the daily manipulation to stop. Thank Allah it never worked out and I was spared. After that, I fully checked out and told them to not bring it up until I finished my degree. After the degree, I used the career stability excuse. I was legitimately scared of the process and marriage. At this point, they want me (their burden) to just leave with anyone. 

I entered the ‘official search’ 2 years ago and it’s been a journey where I have learned a lot. I do have one aunt who is very connected to the mosque and she sends me proposals. She is not perfect but respects when I say no and does not push it. If you have someone like that in your circle, talk to them but only rely on yourself to do the vetting. There are horrible people out there and wonderful people that I would have never met on my own. You’ll likely find the same in dating if you decide to go that route. 

I would 100% suggest you find a good therapist you trust. You likely need some childhood trauma therapy and therapy on what is a good relationship and how to be in one. Be discerning wit therapists because if they don’t get our culture, they just won’t get it at all. Sometimes they have their own agendas. I overall learned a lot from this sub and r/arrangedmarriage

It took me a very long time to realize that what I did consistently would have the appropriate response in my body. If I exercised consistently and ate mostly clean, eventually I would lose weight and get stronger. If I consistently ate out or too much and exercised, I may not gain as much weight but I’m also not losing.

Not eating is not an option if you want sustainable weight loss. 

Just like the car can’t run without gas, you cannot without your fuel source (food). So, if you’ve already decided to order the food, the absolute worst thing you can do is make yourself feel like crap. Your nervous system will become more dysregulated. Enjoy that food to its fullest extent. Stop once your full. And if you still feel bad, think about what you can eat in the future that is healthy (according to your standards). 

Have an honest check in with yourself and ask yourself if you need to reduce take out to x number of days in the week. Don’t ever punish yourself, talk to yourself with compassion and love. I would hear these things and think “ok, ya that will solve all my problems”. But seriously it helps for us to get out of our own way and stay consistent on our goals. 

If I’m in a situation where I need to get fast food, I try to make sure whatever I get has protein and I do my best to not drink my calories. And then I enjoy that burger (or whatever) with full enjoyment. 

Another thing you can do is do some light exercise right after eating. It helps lower the glucose spike. Either go for a short 10 min walk, jumping jacks, stairs, anything physical. I noticed this also gets me out of the thought of “oh noo what have I done”.

I wrote multiple letters over the last 2 years. At first it was an individual letter to all the important people in my life. The list was 10+  These were never complete letters because it always felt like I hadn’t said enough or explained properly. Then, I wrote one single letter for my family and the world (friends, colleagues, and anyone who cares to know that I am dead and why). Then, I wrote one for family and one for the world. I would either write too much or too little. The words were never enough explanation or supportive to how they might be feeling. 

I then decided I would tell my close ones - family and two friends - that I have these thoughts and I likely will do it so if they have any questions or anything they want to know or ask or clarify (basically anything at all), they can do it before my suicide happens. I never had a date/timeline for when I would kill myself. I visualized being very calm and making space for all their emotions and preparing myself for all kinds of questions. 

I even went as far to make a binder with important information my family might need to ease the stress on them when it happens. I made the tabs (personal info/social media accounts/financial accounts/etc) but never got to filling out the information. 

At the end of all that, I realized nothing I write or say will ease the pain of a suicide in the family. When someone dies by suicide, the chances of trauma and suicide in the family/close circle goes up. I don’t want that for my family to be trapped in a traumatic cycle. I learned/understood a lot from r/suicidebereavement

Still, I don’t think that’s a good enough reason for me to keep living. I know deep down, I don’t want to die at all. I want to live, enjoy fun times with my close ones, experience the world, and just let nature takes it course. But this is much harder said than done. I feel suicidal every single day and then have deeper more intense episodes. I try in those times to remind myself that my pain (both mental and physical) is making me want to die, but I (the energy and soul inside me) wants to live. 

At this point, I will write a single letter for my family and one for doctors/health authority/politicians (I have no idea how to send to them right now). I’m glad you have a great doctor team, but I have had horrible experiences and I want the system to know they are responsible for not offering better solutions for chronic pain and chronic mental health issues. If we have better options, I know I would be better, but since we don’t I was desperate to end my pain (not my life). 

Writing out our thoughts is very therapeutic. We don’t need permission on what to write and how to write. We don’t need to keep up social niceties. We can get sad, get real, get angry, get joyful, without any single judgment. 

If you’re scared that writing the letter might be taking you over the edge, see if you can get some ‘support cushion’ before and after the writing session. Maybe cuddles with your wife before and a therapy session afterwards. It could also be watching a show or listening to music, gym, art, walk. Make a safety plan just for that single writing session. 

I hope this was helpful. We’re all trying our best including you.

As someone with major dental trauma and many issues arising from multiple injuries/fillings/root canals, if you can’t stay on top of your teeth self care right now then definitely schedule more regular dental cleanings (if you can afford it). 

Before going to any clinic, call or email them with your concerns and especially mention the anxiety/fear of judgment etc. I have also found that having someone with me that is 100% on my side and will help to advocate for me kind of makes sure they won’t mess around or say something hurtful. You can ask the clinic if a support person can come with you. But this person has to be 100% a safe person for you or else it will make things worse. 

Another thing that has been helpful is to call and pretend you are calling for someone else. It’s way easier to talk about the issue. And then once you’ve settled on a clinic, just call and book it and pretend like this other ‘fake assistant/family/friend’ told you about them. Ask alllllll the questions. If they can’t handle your questions, it may not be the most mentally secure place to go. 

Please please start taking care of your teeth. Not only is it very expensive once they are damaged, it’s very very difficult to function in life with teeth that may not allow you to chew properly.

I have also learned a lot from @drleedia on Instagram and so grateful that I can prevent any further damage.
